name: illustrator-owner-quiz-board-rotated
exporter: Adobe Illustrator - Export As > SVG, Styling: Internal CSS
story: NOT a synthesized fixture: this is the board the owner drew himself on 2026-09-02 and walked, and it is here because it is a real designer's file rather than an imitation of one. A chess-themed quiz card, 1570x700, on a patterned background: a tan question plate holding <text id="question">, and four orange answer plates below it, each holding one unnamed text. Every plate is drawn as a portrait rectangle plus a rotation - the question's is 231x1233 turned -88.68 degrees, painting a 1238x259 band - because he tilted the whole composition on purpose: "my design here is wonky on purpose to see how we manage it when we import it." I claim five text fields, and that the question's own plate is the one a longer question grows, because that is the plate the question is drawn inside.
idioms: every panel written as a rect plus a transform, so its attribute size is the size BEFORE rotation
rotations that are nearly but not exactly a right angle (-88.68, -83.85, 3.92, 6.15, 10.62)
the background pattern supplied as fill:url(#Alyssa) on the backplate, with the motif paths living in <defs>
the question layer named (q_bg, question) while the four answer texts carry no id at all
per-glyph kerning runs: one <text> holding eleven tspans that all share y and step x
one .cls-N class per property, letter-spacing split into its own class
a hand-drawn plate outline as a separate <path> tracing the same rectangle as the filled <rect>
whyThisMatters: Rotated panels are what hand-drawn artwork looks like, and reading a rect's attributes without its transform gets every one of them wrong. Rotation gets one MORE thing wrong than the inventory, found 2026-09-04 by sweeping this file's ladder over all four options and six value lengths: a rect has no width on the screen's axes, so growing this plate's width attribute made the painted band 114 px taller and 2 px wider for a control that says 'the panel gets wider'. The plate also had no room to grow at all, because growth went right and the ceiling mirrored the left margin - and this plate is drawn 212 px in from the left against 120 from the right, which put the ceiling 92 px behind its own right edge. Two more came off the same sweep: a centred block leaves its own panel's line list as soon as a long value widens it past the plate's left edge, so the wrap rung lost its height depending on what had been typed before, and a block the ladder shrank settled 1.5 units below the middle of its box. The three walks that found none of these are in https://github.com/NoaCG/NoaCG-Studio/blob/5098bd923411f74c6a80ac81f4d4e2cb6e871e0b/docs/acceptance/owner-queue/2026-09-02-text-knows-its-box.md; the sweep that did is the last case in e2e/import-svg-corpus.spec.ts. Before 2026-09-02 this file inventoried the question's plate as a tall 231x1233 rectangle, so the growth default picked an answer plate instead and dragged two of the four answers with it, and a long question shrank to 62 percent of the size it was drawn at. The `growth` claim was `grow-y` until 2026-09-02 evening, written from the owner's first sentence about this board (the horizontal fixed, the vertical growing). His fuller ruling the same day supersedes it and is the one recorded in docs/TEXT_BOX_BINDING.md's fit doctrine: a graphic the audience sees again with different content keeps a FIXED box on both axes, and of the quiz specifically, 'it should not grow, because a quiz page should be the same for each question.' The plate has the room for a three-line question at the size it was drawn at, which is what makes the fixed box affordable rather than merely principled. No `growthShape` column: nothing grows, so the step names no shape - which shape it would offer is pinned instead by e2e/import-svg.spec.ts, where the ladder is turned on by hand.
